top3.title: Abronia, Cartoon +Bill Nace, Earthen Jug
top3.why: Portland's Abronia rolls through on the East Coast leg of its tour behind the new LP Shapes Unravel, a shapeshifting blend of desert-noir drone, avant-jazz, doom, and acid-folk that's hard to categorize and harder to skip. The bill is stacked for a random Monday: kraut-punk locals Cartoon, genuinely legendary noise guitarist Bill Nace (Body/Head, decades of free-improv pedigree), and the drone-psych ensemble Earthen Jug. Ortlieb's is a small, no-frills room built for exactly this kind of show, and under $20 covers all four acts.

top3.title: Crooklyn (1994)
top3.why: cinéSPEAK's 'Two Locals Movie Mondays' series brings Spike Lee's Crooklyn — his warm, lived-in portrait of a Brooklyn childhood, anchored by knockout turns from Alfre Woodard and Delroy Lindo — to Philly's first Black-owned brewery. It's a makeup date after a summer reschedule, free to attend with BYO dinner and free popcorn, donations of $5+ welcomed to keep the series running. This is the neighborhood-cinema-meets-community-taproom event that's genuinely easy to miss if you're not watching for it.

top3.title: Sonder x Poison Tree Magazine Launch
top3.why: Two brand-new Philly literary magazines, Sonder and Poison Tree, share a launch party at Tattooed Mom, with early arrivals getting first crack at a collaborative guest book and physical copies of issue one. The back half of the night opens the floor to an open mic — flash fiction, poetry, short essays from whoever wants to read — a genuinely grassroots, no-cover night for anyone plugged into (or curious about) the city's small-press scene.

top3.title: NLG Know Your Rights Training
top3.why: The National Lawyers Guild runs a hands-on know-your-rights training at Wooden Shoe Books, walking attendees through concrete legal footing for encounters with police, ICE, and immigration enforcement. It's the kind of unglamorous, essential organizing work that never trends but matters enormously right now, and hosting it inside Philly's longtime anarchist infoshop on South Street guarantees a room full of people who take it seriously. The listing is thin on specifics beyond time and place, so double-check format and any RSVP requirements before heading over.

top3.title: Touki Bouki
top3.why: Djibril Diop Mambéty's 1973 Senegalese landmark follows a cowherder and a university student scheming to escape postcolonial Dakar for Paris, told in fever-dream imagery with a political charge that hasn't dulled in fifty years — one of the essential works of African and world cinema. It's screening as part of Philadelphia Film Society's summer Road Trip series, a genuinely rare theatrical booking for a film that mostly lives in retrospectives and syllabi, with two showtimes (4:00 and 7:00 PM) presented in Wolof, Arabic, and French with subtitles. No ticket price is listed on this page, so confirm cost through PFS directly.

top3.title: Rolling Quartz
top3.why: South Korean rock band Rolling Quartz — five members deep into riffs sturdier than most K-pop-adjacent crossover acts attempt — bring their "My Turn" reunion tour to PhilaMOCA, a converted mausoleum-turned-DIY art/horror venue about as far from an arena stage as touring bands get. Catching an international act of this scale in a room built for a few hundred people is a genuine rarity, and PhilaMOCA's oddball, community-run character (usually horror screenings and underground art) makes for a memorably strange pairing. Tiered ticketing runs from general admission up through VIP soundcheck/meet-and-greet packages — steep for the venue, but reflective of a real touring draw rather than a local bar band.

top3.title: Noname
top3.why: Noname built her name as one of hip-hop's sharpest political voices, and turned that platform into Noname's Book Club, a radical-lit reading group and prison-literacy program — so a Noname show doubles as a leftist-literary event with a beat. This Fishtown stop marks the 10th anniversary of 'Telefone,' the mixtape that launched her, and it's already sold out — a good sign this is the kind of night people will still be talking about next week. If you don't have a ticket, keep an eye on resale; standing-room GA, all ages.

top3.title: Casket Cassette, with Stare Away, My Manifesto
top3.why: Casket Cassette is Constant Williams' darkwave/coldwave project, splitting the difference between EBM's cold pulse and post-punk gloom — exactly the gothy, danceable dread that belongs in a converted movie theater. This stop on the Reducer Tour lands at PhilaMOCA, the city's reigning home for underground and weird culture, with local support from Stare Away and My Manifesto. $19.13 is cheap for a touring headliner in a room this good.

top3.title: 🔩 Beginner Soldering: Li-Ion Battery Pack
top3.venue: Iffy Books, 404 S. 20th St., Philadelphia, PA 19146
top3.why: A hands-on soldering class at Iffy Books, the West Philly bookstore-slash-hackerspace where DIY electronics and radical lit share shelf space — no prior soldering experience needed. You'll leave with a working rechargeable battery pack fit for a LoRa node, ESP32, or Pi Pico. It's the kind of genuinely useful, easy-to-miss event that only surfaces if you're on Iffy's mailing list: the kit runs about $4, plus a separate 18650 battery, with instructor donations suggested on a notaflof basis.

top3.title: The Body, with BIG|BRAVE, Carnivorous Bells
top3.why: The Body and Big|Brave are two of underground metal's most punishing and inventive acts — The Body fusing doom, noise, and industrial dread with a growing list of unlikely collaborators, Big|Brave bringing droning, hymn-like heaviness that's earned raves from metal and experimental critics alike. It's a rare joint stop on their 2026 North American tour, landing at PhilaMOCA, the city's best home for loud, weird, uncompromising art inside a converted movie-poster warehouse. Doors at 7pm for a 7:30 start, $25 — steep value for a bill this heavy.

top3.title: Pulse (2001)
top3.why: Kiyoshi Kurosawa's 'Pulse' is a genuinely unsettling J-horror landmark — ghosts leaking into Tokyo through dial-up internet and grainy webcams, a film critics now read as eerily prophetic about digital isolation. This is a rare theatrical outing, part of PFS's 'Summer of Trilogies' retrospective on Kurosawa's Terror Trilogy, so it's a real chance to see 25-year-old dread on a real screen instead of a cropped streaming rip. Standalone admission is regular movie-ticket money, or bundle into the three-film pass to go deeper into Kurosawa's paranoid universe.

top3.title: Philly 2600 Meetup
top3.why: Philly 2600 is the local chapter of the international hacker/phreak meetup that's been quietly convening in cities worldwide since the 1980s — an unstructured, drop-in gathering of hackers, phreaks, infosec people, tinkerers, and activists comparing notes. It happens the first Friday of every month at Iffy Books, itself ground zero for DIY electronics, radical politics, and speculative fiction in Philly, so venue and crowd hit the same notes for once. Free, no registration, nothing planned — just show up between 6 and 8:30pm, about as easy to miss and as easy to attend as community events get.

top3.title: The Magic City – Birmingham According To Sun Ra

PhilaMOCA's cavernous former-mausoleum-showroom is the ideal room for a film about a jazz visionary who treated myth and liberation as the same project. $12, one night only — the deepest cut in this week's jazz/soul lineage.

top3.title: Iron Chic
top3.address: 301 S Christopher Columbus Blvd, Philadelphia, PA 19106
top3.why: Long Island melodic-punk mainstays Iron Chic — gruff vocals, huge choruses, songs about hometown malaise and holding on — play a free, all-ages show right on the Delaware waterfront. It's the no-ticket, no-hassle DIY-adjacent show that's easy to scroll past on a Saturday stacked with $40 tribute acts, but it's the real punk pick of the day: doors at 6pm, free, all ages, just show up.

top3.title: 🏴 Anarchy Summer Reading Group: 'The Utopia of Rules' by David Graeber (2nd half)
top3.why: Iffy Books' biweekly anarchist lit circle digs into the back half of David Graeber's 'The Utopia of Rules,' his sly, funny indictment of bureaucracy and structural violence — real political theory, argued out loud with strangers instead of read alone. It's happening in the exact room this kind of conversation belongs in: South Philly's DIY anarchist bookstore, a hub for zines, mutual aid, and radical lit that consistently rewards showing up. No cost beyond your attention, and you don't need to have read the first half to sit in.

top3.title: Inaugural North Philly Transit Rider Union Meeting
top3.why: This is the literal founding meeting of a new SEPTA rider-organizing chapter — the unglamorous, unrepeatable kind of event you'd only catch if you were paying close attention, and exactly the grassroots labor/transit organizing that's easy to miss amid concert listings. It's happening at a public library branch, which is the right venue for a movement built on accessibility. If you care about service cuts, fare hikes, or watching direct democracy assemble itself from a folding table, this is a genuine front-row seat to something just getting started.
